usageNotes: Use this to apply configuration changes to a running service without a full stop/start cycle; Proxmox will automatically fall back to a restart if the service does not support live reload. Requires the `Sys.Modify` privilege on `/nodes/{node}`, so API tokens must carry that permission. The return value is a task UPID — poll the task log to confirm completion.

examples.summary: Reload the Proxmox proxy (pveproxy) on node pve01 to pick up a certificate change

tips: For services that do not natively support SIGHUP-based reload (e.g. corosync), Proxmox will silently fall back to a full restart — treat reload as a best-effort graceful operation.
pveproxy reload is the recommended way to activate a newly installed TLS certificate without dropping active API sessions unnecessarily.
Reloading pvedaemon or pve-cluster during active migrations or HA operations may cause brief task interruptions; prefer a maintenance window.
The returned UPID can be tracked with GET /nodes/{node}/tasks/{upid}/status.
